pathway.title: EnerSys — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage has fallen to a level that leaves wide room, and the only near maturity is covered: net debt over reported EBITDA fell from 1.38x at 2025-12-28 to 0.89x at 2026-10-04 (0.95x pro forma for the buybacks of 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-06), the issuer's own net leverage is 0.8x against the 4.00x maximum last stated for the quarter to 2025-12-28, and cash alone covers the notes due in 2027 0.92 times while cash and committed lines cover them 3.58 times. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2025-12-28_ens.htm.jsonl, page 27; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

Earnings are better than the headline suggests but still lean on a statutory credit: reported EBITDA excluding the production credit rose 58.33% to USD 226.1 million in six months against 44.08% for the reported figure, and the credit's share fell to 28.83% from 35.24%, yet a one-off tariff refund of about USD 29 million also sits in the half year and the annual report says the credits phase out from 2030 and depend on guidance that could change. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 107; calculation C7; calculation C8

Cash conversion is lumpy and should not be annualised: free cash flow was 85.37% of reported EBITDA in fiscal 2024, 24.93% in fiscal 2025 when production credits built up as prepaid taxes, and 109.54% in the six months to 2026-10-04, which includes a USD 115.5 million refund of prior-year taxes; without that refund the figure is 73.18%. Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10

Shareholder returns and growth spending, not leverage, are the swing factor for creditors: buybacks and dividends took 85.96% of free cash flow excluding the tax refund in six months, the company has announced about USD 820 million of acquisition and plant spending, and the Ultralife enterprise value of about USD 320 million is above cash of USD 275.5 million, so funding from cash on hand depends on cash built before closing. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C12

Demand is diversified and shifting toward defense and data centers, but forklift weakness is real: Precision Power Solutions sales rose 22.3% and Network & Infrastructure Solutions sales rose 6.2% in six months while Industrial Mobility Solutions sales fell 5.6%, no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, and order backlog is not stated, so visibility rests on the quarterly outlook of net sales between USD 935 million and USD 975 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; calculation C14

Margins carry commodity and currency exposure that is only partly passed through: about 20% of revenue is priced to lead with a six to nine month lag, a 10% rise in lead cost would have added about USD 32 million to six-month cost of goods sold, 9% of fiscal-year lead needs were hedged at 2026-10-04, and about 40% of sales and expenses are in foreign currencies. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C15

Claims outside reported debt are small beside earnings: at 2025-03-31 operating lease liabilities were USD 89,388 thousand, the retirement plan deficit USD 22,481 thousand and purchase commitments USD 21.5 million, and the receivables program moves the timing of cash rather than adding debt, though a lapse would tie up cash in receivables. Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 136; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C16

runs.text: Strength 1, low leverage and a light maturity wall: net debt was 0.89x reported EBITDA (0.95x pro forma for the buybacks of 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-06), and after the notes due in 2027 the next contractual maturity is the revolver on 2030-09-30, so refinancing pressure is limited to one USD 300.0 million repayment, which cash and committed lines cover 3.58 times, apart from USD 28,661 thousand of short-term bank borrowings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 38; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4

Strength 2, a diversified customer base with growth where demand is strongest: no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, and defense and data center growth is offsetting weaker forklift demand, which protects total sales from a single end market. Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C13

Strength 3, underlying earnings improvement beyond the credit: reported EBITDA excluding the production credit rose 58.33% in six months and operating expenses fell to 15.9% of net sales from 17.7%, which shows cost actions are reaching earnings and lowers the credit's weight in coverage. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C21

Strength 4, cash generation that repaid debt: the revolver principal fell by USD 294,563 thousand in six months and free cash flow excluding the tax refund was 73.18% of reported EBITDA, so debt reduction and buybacks were funded from operating cash flow and cash on hand, not net borrowing. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C10; calculation C17

Strength 5, no sponsor or controlling holder: related-party transactions are stated as none and the statements are audited with effective internal control, so no owner extracts value ahead of creditors. Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 94; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness 1, cash allocation: buybacks and dividends took 85.96% of free cash flow excluding the tax refund, USD 769,996,837 of authorization remains, and about USD 820 million of acquisition and plant spending is announced, so cash can leave faster than debt is repaid, and the credit agreement limits on this are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 59; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C12

Weakness 2, earnings that lean on credits and refunds: production credits supplied 28.83% of six-month reported EBITDA and a tariff refund added about USD 29 million, so a policy change or the end of the refund would cut EBITDA and coverage. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 107; calculation C8

Weakness 3, cyclical forklift and truck demand: Industrial Mobility Solutions sales fell 5.6% and organic volume fell 5% in six months as customers paused larger purchases, and this segment is 42.7% of net sales. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13

Weakness 4, commodity, currency and price exposure: lead is the largest raw material cost, 9% of lead needs were hedged, competitors that own smelters can price more freely when lead rises, and a 10% lead rise would have cost about USD 32 million in six months. Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C15

Weakness 5, technology and execution risk: the company states it cannot assure that its mainly lead-acid portfolio stays competitive with new technologies, and the cell plant needs about USD 500 million of net investment funded from operating cash flow with full production about three years after construction starts. Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The pending acquisition of Ultralife is a cash tender offer at USD 16.00 per share, an enterprise value of about USD 320 million, announced on 2026-10-27 and expected to close in the first quarter of calendar 2027 if a majority of shares are tendered and regulatory approvals are received. EnerSys expects to fund it with cash on hand, which the company says would reduce its cash balance; no amount is recognised in the statements at 2026-10-04, and the effect on net debt is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39

No new notes or term loans were issued in the six months to 2026-10-04. The debt issues in the period covered are the 6.625% notes due 2032, issued on 2024-01-11 for USD 300 million, and the sixth amendment to the credit facility in the fiscal second quarter of 2026, which raised the revolver to USD 1.0 billion, extended its maturity to 2030-09-30 and repaid the term loans. The 4.375% notes due 2027, USD 300 million, are the next maturity. Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2025-12-28_ens.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 38

The company also amended its receivables purchase agreement on 2025-12-15 to a maximum of USD 250 million plus an uncommitted USD 50 million accordion, maturing 2028-12-15, and plans a lithium-ion cell plant costing about USD 650 million with a DOE grant of about USD 150 million, leaving net investment of about USD 500 million to be funded from operating cash flow. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for EnerSys (issuer ens-1289308), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage on the issuer's consolidated perimeter, from the annual report for fiscal 2025 to the quarter ended 2026-10-04.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EnerSys has low leverage and ample liquidity, so creditors are well covered: net debt was 0.89x twelve-month reported EBITDA at 2026-10-04, down from 1.38x at 2025-12-28, and USD 1,073.83 million of cash and committed lines is 3.58 times the notes due in 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX99.1_2025-12-28_ens_ex991-earningsx3qfy26-htm.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation N6; calculation S5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk is how cash is used, not leverage today: the company spent USD 180.0 million on buybacks in the half year and about USD 40 million more since quarter end, has agreed to buy Ultralife at an enterprise value of about USD 320 million to be funded from cash on hand, and gets 28.83% of half-year reported EBITDA from the IRC 45X credit. Cash interest cover was 11.44x in fiscal 2025 but is not supplied since, and covenant terms after fiscal 2025 are only partly established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 123; calculation S1; calculation S8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt at carrying value rose from 1.15x reported EBITDA at 2024-03-31 to 1.38x at 2025-03-31 and was still 1.38x at 2025-12-28, because the fiscal 2025 acquisitions, share repurchases and a build in prepaid taxes were funded in part on the revolver, which had net borrowing of USD 280.0 million in the year. It fell to 0.87x at 2026-07-05 and 0.89x at 2026-10-04 as twelve-month reported EBITDA rose to USD 608.6 million and gross debt fell by 30.90% from 2025-12-28.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation S2; calculation S4; calculation N1; calculation N2; calculation N3; calculation N5; calculation N6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 9.03x in fiscal 2024 and 11.44x in fiscal 2025. Cash interest paid is stated for fiscal years only, so later cover rests on a proxy on twelve-month interest expense, 13.29x at 2026-10-04, which is a different measure and is labelled as one. The issuer's own net leverage of 0.8x against a 4.00x maximum shows wide headroom on its definitions, but covenant levels after fiscal 2025 other than the 4.00x leverage level are not established, so headroom under the covenants cannot be calculated here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt flatters domestic leverage, because a substantial majority of cash is held by foreign subsidiaries and is considered indefinitely reinvested while the senior notes are obligations of the parent company. Leverage could also rise again if the cash-funded Ultralife purchase and the buybacks continue, because the half year's operating cash flow included USD 115.5 million of one-off tax refunds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow fell to USD 260.3 million in fiscal 2025 from USD 457.0 million because the production credits were booked as prepaid taxes, which rose by USD 192.1 million, before being collected; the half year to 2026-10-04 then produced USD 372.8 million, of which an IRS refund of prior-year taxes supplied USD 115.5 million, after USD 137.0 million in the prior-year half. Operating cash flow therefore follows the credit-collection cycle and is not a clean run rate. Capital expenditure was 1.32% of net sales in the half year against 3.35% in fiscal 2025, while the company's own outlook is about USD 70 million for the year, so free cash flow would be lower in the second half if the outlook holds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 52; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation S7; calculation S11; calculation S12; calculation S13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash of USD 275.5 million plus undrawn committed facilities of USD 798.33 million gives USD 1,073.83 million, 3.58 times the USD 300.0 million 4.375% notes that mature on 2027-12-15 and will be current debt from the quarter ending 2027-01-03. The revolver, USD 193.0 million drawn of a USD 1,000 million commitment, matures on 2030-09-30 and the 2032 notes on 2032-01-15, so no other contractual maturity falls before fiscal 2031; the availability of the revolver is subject to the credit agreement financial covenants.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 120; calculation L6; calculation S5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company also funds itself through a receivables purchase program: it sold USD 682.504 million of receivables in the half year and USD 775.236 million in fiscal 2025, all collected by the dates reported, and receivables of USD 372.887 million held by EnerSys Finance would likely not be available to other creditors in an insolvency until the purchasers are repaid. A lapse of the program, which matures on 2028-12-15, would tie up cash in receivables.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA is the primary denominator and adjusted EBITDA per credit agreement is a separate row; the two adjusted measures the issuer publishes, its company adjusted EBITDA and the credit-agreement figure, are never mixed, and the first-quarter fiscal 2027 company figure differs between two releases. Carrying-value net debt differs from the issuer's credit-agreement net debt by the unamortized issuance costs and standby letters of credit, with a small residual, as the definition register sets out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The annual report for fiscal 2026 is not supplied, so fiscal 2026 EBITDA and cash interest are gaps and fiscal 2026 net sales is assembled from four printed quarters. The segment structure changed on 2026-05-28, so fiscal 2024 and 2025 segment sales are on the four-segment basis and are not joined to the three-segment half-year figures.

fields.value: Events after 2026-10-04 are kept out of the period figures: share repurchases of about USD 40 million, which would lift net leverage to 0.95x, the dividend payable on 2026-12-31 and the pending Ultralife acquisition, whose effect on net debt is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The annual report for fiscal 2026 and the fourth-quarter release are not supplied, so fiscal 2026 EBITDA, cash interest paid, cash flow and the debt note are not stated, and leverage and cover at 2026-03-31 cannot be worked; only the balance sheet and fourth-quarter net sales are available, and the prior period named in the run settings is therefore only partly covered. Severity: High. Action: supply the annual report filed on 2026-05-20.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid and income taxes paid are stated for fiscal years only, so interim cover on cash interest is not calculable and the register carries a labelled proxy on twelve-month interest expense. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the interim cash flow supplemental disclosures or the fiscal 2026 annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels after fiscal 2025 are not established beyond the 4.00x maximum leverage level, and the minimum interest coverage level is not restated, so headroom under the covenants cannot be calculated. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the executed credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The guarantor subsidiaries of the senior notes and the credit facility are not named, and the legal rank of short-term borrowings is not stated, so short-term borrowings are left out of the debt stack and the maturity ladder. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the indentures, the credit agreement and the list of subsidiaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The effect of the Ultralife acquisition on net debt is not stated: the enterprise value of about USD 320 million is given but not the equity price, Ultralife's own debt and cash, or any financing beyond cash on hand, so no pro forma net debt or leverage is stated for it. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the merger agreement, the tender offer documents and Ultralife's financial statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Two adjusted EBITDA measures are published, company adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA per credit agreement, and first-quarter fiscal 2027 company adjusted EBITDA is 195.8 in one release but 195.2 as implied by another; adjusted EBITDA per credit agreement is stated for twelve-month periods only, so the half-year columns of the adjusted EBITDA row are gaps. Severity: Medium. Action: state which measure each ratio uses and keep the two separate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The total of the quarterly dividend payable on 2026-12-31 is not stated, only the rate per share, so its effect on net debt is not stated; the dividend at the same rate in the quarter to 2026-10-04 was 10.298 US$m. Severity: Low. Action: supply the share count at the record date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lines printed as a dash in the statements are treated as missing, not zero, and lines that an interim statement does not present are gaps in the half-year columns. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for credit use; the figures concerned are small or absent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Finance lease obligations are not presented separately after 2025-03-31, so the finance lease amount inside the issuer's credit-agreement net debt cannot be separated, and a residual of 0.053 US$m between the rebuilt and reported net debt at 2026-10-04 is unexplained. Severity: Low. Action: supply the lease note.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Balance sheets at 2025-06-29 and 2025-09-28 are not supplied, so net debt and its ratios are not stated for the half year to 2025-09-28, and net sales for fiscal 2026 and for the interim twelve-month periods rest on a fourth-quarter figure printed to one decimal. Severity: Low. Action: supply the first and second quarter reports of fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not split; only total capital expenditure is stated. Severity: Low. Action: supply the split if it exists.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, ownership, governance and transaction fact pack for EnerSys (issuer ens-1289308), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the operating model, ownership and control, capital allocation and the pending Ultralife acquisition, from the annual report for fiscal 2025 to the quarter ended 2026-10-04.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EnerSys is a widely held industrial battery maker with no controlling owner or sponsor named, so the creditor risk is how management uses cash, not extraction by an owner: buybacks, a cash-funded Ultralife purchase and a large cell plant compete with debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sales are diversified, with no customer above 10% of revenue, and defense and data center growth is offsetting weaker forklift and truck demand, but half-year profit leans on production tax credits worth 28.83% of reported EBITDA and a one-off tariff refund of about USD 29 million. Board, holder and compensation detail is not established because the proxy statement was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C1; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration is not a credit risk: no customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue, and sales are spread across many end markets and countries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The mix is moving toward defense and data center demand and away from forklift batteries: in the six months to 2026-10-04 Precision Power sales rose 22.3% and Network & Infrastructure sales rose 6.2%, while Industrial Mobility sales fell 5.6% on a 5% fall in organic volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported profit growth is flattered by items outside the operating franchise: production tax credits supplied 28.83% of six-month reported EBITDA and a tariff refund added about USD 29 million, and both helped lift gross margin to 31.7% from 28.8%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash use is the governance risk that matters: the company bought back USD 180.0 million of shares in six months, has USD 769,996,837 of authorization left, which is 2.79 times its cash, and has announced about USD 820 million of acquisition and plant spending, so debt reduction is not the only claim on cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 59; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality supports creditor monitoring but control detail is missing: the statements are audited with effective internal control, related-party transactions are stated as none and no sponsor is named, yet board, holder and compensation detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the chief executive changed after the 2025 annual report without a supplied explanation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 153; EX99.1_2025-12-28_ens_ex991-earningsx3qfy26-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditor treatment looks aligned so far: the sixth amendment raised the revolver by USD 150 million, extended its maturity to 2030-09-30 and repaid the term loans, and no uptier, exchange or waiver is stated, but the legal capacity for distributions is not tested because the credit agreement was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has acted on cost: a reduction in force of about 11% of non-production staff cost USD 21,651 thousand, and operating expenses fell to 15.9% of net sales from 17.7%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading cash use as the main risk is the half-year record: the company repaid revolver debt out of operating cash flow while also buying back shares, no owner stands behind a leveraged distribution, and the acquisition is described as funded from cash on hand. The view would change if the Ultralife purchase or the buybacks were funded with new borrowing, if the proxy statement showed a holder with control or veto rights, or if the credits and refunds that lifted gross margin stopped, which would show how much of the profit growth is organic. It would also change if the credit agreement allowed distributions at levels that cash flow could not cover.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 41; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so board, large holders and compensation are not established; this limits the conclusion that no controlling or sponsor owner exists to the holders the filings name.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so legal capacity for buybacks and acquisitions is not established; the conclusion that cash use is the main risk rests on observed behaviour, not on tested capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The merger agreement and Ultralife's own statements are not supplied, so the acquisition's financing and its effect on net debt are not established; the conclusion that it is cash-funded rests on the company's statement alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment data on the new three-segment basis exists for fiscal 2026 and later only, so the conclusion on the shift in mix covers two half years, not a full cycle.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The reason and date of the change of chief executive are not established, so continuity of financial policy under new leadership cannot be tested.

fields.value: The registers and report tables that follow hold every figure and trace behind the findings above.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The pending acquisition of Ultralife is a cash tender offer at USD 16.00 per share, an enterprise value of about USD 320 million, announced on 2026-10-27 and expected to close in the first quarter of calendar 2027 if a majority of shares are tendered and regulatory approvals are received. EnerSys expects to fund it with cash on hand, which the company says would reduce its cash balance; no amount is recognised in the statements at 2026-10-04, and the effect on net debt is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new notes or term loans were issued in the six months to 2026-10-04. The debt issues in the period covered are the 6.625% notes due 2032, issued on 2024-01-11 for USD 300 million, and the sixth amendment to the credit facility in the fiscal second quarter of 2026, which raised the revolver to USD 1.0 billion, extended its maturity to 2030-09-30 and repaid the term loans. The 4.375% notes due 2027, USD 300 million, are the next maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company also amended its receivables purchase agreement on 2025-12-15 to a maximum of USD 250 million plus an uncommitted USD 50 million accordion, maturing 2028-12-15, and plans a lithium-ion cell plant costing about USD 650 million with a DOE grant of about USD 150 million, leaving net investment of about USD 500 million to be funded from operating cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by large and rising shareholder distributions and cash-funded growth, because they use cash that could repay debt, which implies moderate pressure on leverage if the pace continues. Countervailing evidence is the revolver repayment from operating cash flow, the absence of any sponsor, related-party or creditor-adverse action, and audited reporting.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of EnerSys (issuer ens-1289308), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business risk, financial profile, financial policy, outlook, downside path and monitoring triggers, drawn from the supplied filings to the quarter ended 2026-10-04 and the three earlier modules of this run.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EnerSys has a strong fundamental credit profile on leverage and liquidity, so creditors are well covered today: net debt was 0.89x twelve-month reported EBITDA at 2026-10-04, or 0.95x pro forma for about USD 40 million of buybacks between 2026-10-05 and 2026-11-06.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk is how cash is used and how earnings are built: buybacks of USD 180.0 million in six months, the pending Ultralife purchase and a cell plant compete with debt reduction, and production tax credits supplied 28.83% of six-month reported EBITDA. The effect of the Ultralife purchase and the December dividend on net debt is not established. Cash and committed lines of USD 1,073.83 million cover the USD 300.0 million notes due in 2027 3.58 times.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C4; calculation C8; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has fallen to a level that leaves wide room, and the only near maturity is covered: net debt over reported EBITDA fell from 1.38x at 2025-12-28 to 0.89x at 2026-10-04 (0.95x pro forma for the buybacks of 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-06), the issuer's own net leverage is 0.8x against the 4.00x maximum last stated for the quarter to 2025-12-28, and cash alone covers the notes due in 2027 0.92 times while cash and committed lines cover them 3.58 times.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2025-12-28_ens.htm.jsonl, page 27; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are better than the headline suggests but still lean on a statutory credit: reported EBITDA excluding the production credit rose 58.33% to USD 226.1 million in six months against 44.08% for the reported figure, and the credit's share fell to 28.83% from 35.24%, yet a one-off tariff refund of about USD 29 million also sits in the half year and the annual report says the credits phase out from 2030 and depend on guidance that could change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 107; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.value: Cash conversion is lumpy and should not be annualised: free cash flow was 85.37% of reported EBITDA in fiscal 2024, 24.93% in fiscal 2025 when production credits built up as prepaid taxes, and 109.54% in the six months to 2026-10-04, which includes a USD 115.5 million refund of prior-year taxes; without that refund the figure is 73.18%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns and growth spending, not leverage, are the swing factor for creditors: buybacks and dividends took 85.96% of free cash flow excluding the tax refund in six months, the company has announced about USD 820 million of acquisition and plant spending, and the Ultralife enterprise value of about USD 320 million is above cash of USD 275.5 million, so funding from cash on hand depends on cash built before closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand is diversified and shifting toward defense and data centers, but forklift weakness is real: Precision Power Solutions sales rose 22.3% and Network & Infrastructure Solutions sales rose 6.2% in six months while Industrial Mobility Solutions sales fell 5.6%, no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, and order backlog is not stated, so visibility rests on the quarterly outlook of net sales between USD 935 million and USD 975 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins carry commodity and currency exposure that is only partly passed through: about 20% of revenue is priced to lead with a six to nine month lag, a 10% rise in lead cost would have added about USD 32 million to six-month cost of goods sold, 9% of fiscal-year lead needs were hedged at 2026-10-04, and about 40% of sales and expenses are in foreign currencies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside reported debt are small beside earnings: at 2025-03-31 operating lease liabilities were USD 89,388 thousand, the retirement plan deficit USD 22,481 thousand and purchase commitments USD 21.5 million, and the receivables program moves the timing of cash rather than adding debt, though a lapse would tie up cash in receivables.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 136; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against treating cash use and credit dependence as the main risks is the half-year record: operating cash flow and cash on hand repaid USD 294,563 thousand of revolver principal while also funding buybacks, reported EBITDA excluding the credit still rose 58.33%, and even if the credit's share of twelve-month EBITDA matched the six-month 28.83% (the fourth-quarter guidance implies 26.83% to 27.65%), net debt over EBITDA would be about 1.25x with interest cover of 9.46x on a proxy basis. The view would turn more negative if net debt over reported EBITDA returned to the 1.38x of fiscal 2025 after Ultralife and further buybacks, if the Ultralife purchase or buybacks were funded by drawing the revolver, or if the production credits were cut before the 2030 phase-out the annual report describes. It would turn more positive if the notes due in 2027 were repaid or refinanced without drawing the revolver and the fiscal 2026 results confirmed the half-year trend.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 107; EX99.1_2025-12-28_ens_ex991-earningsx3qfy26-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX99.1_2025-12-28_ens_ex991-earningsx3qfy26-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C17; calculation C24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The fiscal 2026 annual report is not supplied, so the conclusion on cash conversion rests on fiscal 2024, fiscal 2025 and two half years, and a full-year fiscal 2026 margin or cash flow could move it either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels and headroom after fiscal 2025 are not established, so the liquidity conclusion counts the undrawn revolver as available without a covenant test and would weaken if headroom proved narrow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No current order backlog, book-to-bill ratio or contract term is stated, so the conclusion that revenue is durable rests on reported sales trends and management's outlook, and is weakest for the project-driven data center and defense lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The twelve-month production credit is not reported because the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 is only guided at USD 37 million to USD 42 million, so the leverage illustration without the credit scales the six-month share and could be off by a small amount in either direction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2025-12-28_ens_ex991-earningsx3qfy26-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C9; calculation C24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating, bond price or peer data is supplied, so the conclusion on market access and the comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector rests on balance sheet strength alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The registers and report tables that follow hold every figure and trace behind the findings above.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength 1, low leverage and a light maturity wall: net debt was 0.89x reported EBITDA (0.95x pro forma for the buybacks of 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-06), and after the notes due in 2027 the next contractual maturity is the revolver on 2030-09-30, so refinancing pressure is limited to one USD 300.0 million repayment, which cash and committed lines cover 3.58 times, apart from USD 28,661 thousand of short-term bank borrowings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 38; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength 2, a diversified customer base with growth where demand is strongest: no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, and defense and data center growth is offsetting weaker forklift demand, which protects total sales from a single end market.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength 3, underlying earnings improvement beyond the credit: reported EBITDA excluding the production credit rose 58.33% in six months and operating expenses fell to 15.9% of net sales from 17.7%, which shows cost actions are reaching earnings and lowers the credit's weight in coverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 41; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength 4, cash generation that repaid debt: the revolver principal fell by USD 294,563 thousand in six months and free cash flow excluding the tax refund was 73.18% of reported EBITDA, so debt reduction and buybacks were funded from operating cash flow and cash on hand, not net borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C10; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength 5, no sponsor or controlling holder: related-party transactions are stated as none and the statements are audited with effective internal control, so no owner extracts value ahead of creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness 1, cash allocation: buybacks and dividends took 85.96% of free cash flow excluding the tax refund, USD 769,996,837 of authorization remains, and about USD 820 million of acquisition and plant spending is announced, so cash can leave faster than debt is repaid, and the credit agreement limits on this are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 59; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness 2, earnings that lean on credits and refunds: production credits supplied 28.83% of six-month reported EBITDA and a tariff refund added about USD 29 million, so a policy change or the end of the refund would cut EBITDA and coverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 107; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness 3, cyclical forklift and truck demand: Industrial Mobility Solutions sales fell 5.6% and organic volume fell 5% in six months as customers paused larger purchases, and this segment is 42.7% of net sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, pages 40–41; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness 4, commodity, currency and price exposure: lead is the largest raw material cost, 9% of lead needs were hedged, competitors that own smelters can price more freely when lead rises, and a 10% lead rise would have cost about USD 32 million in six months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness 5, technology and execution risk: the company states it cannot assure that its mainly lead-acid portfolio stays competitive with new technologies, and the cell plant needs about USD 500 million of net investment funded from operating cash flow with full production about three years after construction starts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is average: the customer base is broad and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, but the largest segments are cyclical or project-driven, so sales can swing by segment even when the total is stable; net sales rose 2.2% in six months on a 1% price rise and a 1% rise in organic volume while the second quarter was flat at USD 949.9 million because of currency.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is partial: about 20% of revenue follows a lead index with a six to nine month lag, the annual report records pricing pressure from excess capacity and consolidation among purchasers, and management says selling prices should be higher on average in fiscal 2027 than in fiscal 2026, so price recovers cost only after a delay.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth quarter is the strongest and the second quarter the weakest, so interim leverage and cash flow are not a full-year run rate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin resilience is average: gross margin rose to 31.7% from 28.8% in six months, but the company attributes the rise mainly to the production credit and tariff refunds, and in the second quarter gross margin excluding the credit was 25.2%, only 30 basis points higher than a year earlier, so organic margin gains are modest and the larger step-up would reverse if the credit or the refund ended.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost flexibility is helped by actions already taken: operating expenses fell to 15.9% of net sales from 17.7%, the 2025 reduction in force cost USD 21,651 thousand, and the closure of the Tijuana lead-acid plant, which the company says is meant to maximize production tax benefits and reduce tariff risk, carries a pre-tax charge of about USD 37,000 thousand of which about USD 23,000 thousand is cash, with completion expected by December 2027, so fixed cost falls but cash is spent first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow stability is weak to average: capital expenditure was 1.32% of net sales in six months against 3.35% in fiscal 2025 and the annual outlook is about USD 70 million, so the second half must spend more than the first, and operating cash flow depends on collecting the prepaid taxes that production credits created.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 97; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Working capital improved: primary operating capital fell to 22.0% of annualized net sales from 26.5% a year earlier, but part of the fall comes from receivables sold under the purchase program, and the program sold USD 682,504 thousand of receivables in six months, so the gain is partly a shift of funding off the balance sheet and reverses if the program lapses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C16; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the weakest dimension: the company is public with no controlling holder or sponsor named, which removes owner extraction, but management has set a USD 1.0 billion buyback authorization, raised the quarterly dividend to USD 0.2875 per share from USD 0.2625 and announced a cash-funded acquisition and a large plant, so policy is shareholder-oriented and its legal limits are not tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 59; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions are a sustained policy, not a one-off: thirty-six acquisitions were made between fiscal 2003 and 2025, including Bren-Tronics for USD 206.4 million in cash in 2024, so integration cost and goodwill risk recur; creditor treatment has been aligned so far because the sixth credit amendment extended maturities and no uptier or exchange is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high: rivals in lead-acid include East Penn, Exide and Hoppecke, excess capacity and purchaser consolidation have caused pricing pressure, and some rivals own lead smelters, which gives them a cost edge when lead rises; the effect on creditors is margin pressure that the lead index covers only for about 20% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is moderate: the company believes a significant capital investment is needed to make thin plate pure lead batteries, but lithium cell packagers and forklift manufacturers are entering larger motive power batteries, which puts Industrial Mobility Solutions share and price at risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes is rising: the company cannot assure that its mainly lead-acid portfolio stays competitive with new technologies, and it reports its first order for its DataSafe Noir lithium solution and sales from a second-generation lithium offering for material handling, so conversion spending and the cell plant are part of defending revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is moderate: no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, which limits any single buyer's leverage, but consolidation among industrial battery purchasers and forklift manufacturers that integrate batteries concentrate bargaining strength in material handling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is moderate: lead is bought from many suppliers and partly hedged, but the commodity price moves with the market, copper and antimony prices rose in fiscal 2027, and the annual report records exposure to battery cell price swings and supply shortages, so cost spikes reach margin before price follows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy is a primary credit driver: the production credit is described as available from 2023 to 2032 with phase-out beginning in 2030 and subject to guidance that could change, tariffs struck down by the Supreme Court in February 2026 produced a refund of about USD 29 million in the half year, and the Tijuana closure was framed partly around the credit and tariff risk, so policy changes move EBITDA directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-03-31_ens.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Currency, defense budgets and rates matter second: about 40% of sales and expenses are in foreign currencies, mainly the euro, the second-quarter sales shortfall against guidance came from currency, defense budgets are rising, and the revolver is floating-rate, which is 23.49% of principal, while the senior notes are fixed-rate at 73.02%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 56; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths in credit terms are low leverage, a diversified customer base and no sponsor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses are reliance on production credits and refunds, cyclical forklift demand and commodity exposure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are continued defense and data center growth and a material handling recovery that management expects to return Industrial Mobility Solutions to growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats that could weaken credit quality are an earlier end to the production credits, leverage-funded buybacks or acquisitions, and lithium competition in motive power.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and diversification are strengths, margin stability and free cash flow stability are average, liquidity and access to capital markets are strong on the balance sheet, and financial policy is the weakest dimension; the trend is better, with net debt over reported EBITDA down from 1.38x to 0.89x (0.95x pro forma for the buybacks of 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-06), and the missing datapoints are fiscal 2026 full-year results, covenant levels after fiscal 2025, a credit rating and the Ultralife funding terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The next 12 to 24 months are supportive for revenue and neutral for cash: management guides the quarter to 2027-01-03 to net sales of USD 935 million to USD 975 million, which is 1.73% to 6.08% above the prior-year third quarter, expects material handling to start recovering, and excludes Ultralife and tariff refunds from its outlook; against that, Industrial Mobility Solutions margin is expected to come under pressure as transportation outgrows material handling, and the notes due in 2027 fall due on 2027-12-15.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2025-12-28_ens.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 3 to 5 years the plant and the tax credits dominate: construction in Greenville is expected to begin in the first half of fiscal 2028 with full production about three years later, net investment is about USD 500 million, the revolver matures on 2030-09-30, and the annual report says the production credit begins to phase out in 2030, so the plant's cash needs overlap with the period when the credit support starts to fade.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tailwinds are data center and defense demand and a communications recovery, which are less sensitive to tariff policy; headwinds are forklift and Class 8 truck demand, lead and freight costs, currency and tariff uncertainty.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path starts with forklift and truck demand staying weak while the production credit is cut or phased down earlier than expected and lead prices rise: Industrial Mobility Solutions, 42.7% of net sales, would shrink further, losing the credit would raise cost of sales by an amount equal to 28.83% of six-month reported EBITDA, and a 10% rise in lead cost would add about USD 32 million per six months before prices catch up six to nine months later.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C8; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial transmission is cushioned: if the credit's share of twelve-month EBITDA matched the six-month share, EBITDA would be about USD 433.1 million and net debt would be about 1.25x it, with interest cover of 9.46x on the proxy basis, and without the tariff refund of about USD 29 million net debt would be 0.93x EBITDA, so leverage rises but stays far below the 4.00x maximum last stated on the issuer's definition, which the credit agreement lets rise temporarily to 4.50x for four quarters after an acquisition larger than USD 250 million, a size the Ultralife enterprise value of about USD 320 million exceeds although whether it qualifies is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2025-12-28_ens.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The liquidity and refinancing effect is limited unless cash leaves at the same time: cash and committed lines of USD 1,073.83 million cover the USD 300.0 million notes due in 2027 3.58 times, but cash alone covers them 0.92 times, the Ultralife purchase and buybacks draw on the same cash, and revolver availability depends on covenants that are not established, so distress needs both a sharp earnings fall and heavy cash outflows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 39; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management levers are the pace of buybacks, the dividend, the timing of the plant, capital expenditure and revolver drawings; observable triggers are third-quarter net sales below the outlook range, gross margin excluding the credit below the second-quarter level of 25.2%, revolver drawings above USD 193.0 million and no plan for the 2027 notes by the quarter ending 2027-01-03. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress on the supplied evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-10-04_ens_ex991-earningsx2qfy27-htm.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-04_ens.htm.jsonl, page 22; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, EnerSys presents an adequate business profile supported by a diversified customer base, defense and data center growth and no sponsor, but credit quality is constrained by cash use and by earnings that lean on production credits and a tariff refund. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow conversion ranged from 24.93% to 109.54% and was 73.18% in the latest half year without the tax refund. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the cash left after buybacks, Ultralife and the plant, since cash and committed lines cover the notes due in 2027 3.58 times. The primary downside path is a cut in the credits and weak forklift demand while cash leaves through buybacks and acquisitions. Further analysis would require the fiscal 2026 annual report, the credit agreement, the Ultralife terms and peer data, because no peer or rating evidence is supplied to compare EnerSys with typical leveraged-credit issuers in its sector. Top risk: cash leaving the company through buybacks and acquisitions while earnings rely on production credits.
